Guidance & outlook: The Bank reported its highest-ever Profit After Tax (PAT) of `9,513 crore for FY 2025-26, registering a growth of 27% over the previous financial year.
Trust-Led xxiv IDBI Bank has enrolled more than 2 Lakh subscribers under APY for FY 2024-25, against Annual Target of 1.38 lakh subscribers.
The Bank's Net Profit increased to ` 9,513 crore for FY 2025-26, registering a robust growth of 27% over FY 2024-25.
Growth & demand: Deposits registered a robust growth of 23% year-on-year to `3.47 lakh crore, while advances grew by 16% year-on-year to `2.53 lakh crore.
Against this backdrop, India remained the fastest-growing major economy, registering an annualised growth of 7.7% in FY 2025-26 as per the Provisional Estimates (PE) released in June 2026.
On the lending side, net advances grew by a robust 16% to ` 2,53,626 crore, supported by balanced credit growth.
Margins & costs: Macroeconomic Overview The global economy during FY 2025- 26 continued to navigate an evolving macroeconomic environment shaped by geopolitical uncertainties, shifting trade dynamics, moderating inflationary trends, and changing monetary policy cycles across major economies.

Maintaining its retail-centric focus, the Bank continued to strengthen its liability franchise through growth in low-cost deposits and diversified term deposit base, while also expanding its well-balanced asset portfolio.
The CASA ratio remained healthy at 44.59%, reflecting a stable and cost-effective funding profile.
Capex & expansion: Domestic economic activity benefited from sustained bank credit growth, higher capacity utilisation, healthy balance sheets of banks and corporates and continued thrust on capital expenditure by the Government.
The Bank also leveraged its dedicated Project Appraisal Cell for the evaluation of greenfield and brownfield corporate projects, thereby supporting fee-based income growth.

The Bank upgraded CBS hardware, expanded network capacity with dual connectivity across more than 98% of its branches, established public cloud landing zones, refreshed end-user computing infrastructure and enhanced cyber resilience through the rollout of an enterprise-wide Extended Detection and Response - Endpoint Detection and Response (XDR-EDR) platform.
Balance sheet & cash: Our commitment to this narrative is best illustrated by several key digital and operational milestones: i-MSME Express : An innovative digital underwriting platform that leverages real-time data ecosystems to assess borrower profiles, enabling swift, hassle-free, and collateral-free credit delivery to micro, small, and medium enterprises.

Your Bank's Leverage Ratio as on March 31, 2026 was 10.51% as against the minimum regulatory requirement of 3.50%.
Risks & challenges: The Bank received the ET BFSI 2025 Award for Excellence in Security and Fraud Risk Management, reflecting its strong governance, advanced risk management frameworks and proactive measures to safeguard customers and systems.

While global uncertainties and geopolitical risks continue to pose challenges, India's strong domestic demand, policy credibility and structural reforms position the economy well to sustain healthy growth momentum.

The Bank continued to maintain a prudent portfolio mix, with retail advances accounting for 70% and corporate advances accounted for 30% of its advances, thereby reinforcing portfolio granularity and risk diversification.
